expectations.evidence: Amended, no new file: tickets.md gains TKT-014..TKT-018 (lines 128-165) and cli.md gains CLI-010..CLI-014 (lines 77-123); CLI-001 and CLI-006 are edited in place. expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro, one paragraph at tickets.md:92-95: 'An agent sees which tickets ran past their due time without doing date arithmetic, and can list only those tickets. The ticket that has been due longest comes first in that listing...' (a TODO status paragraph follows). 'Prefix: `TKT`.' at tickets.md:12, 'Prefix: `CLI`.' at cli.md:8. 'Non-goals:' at tickets.md:109 with 9 boundaries, e.g. 'No notification, reminder, or escalation when a ticket becomes overdue.' (114), 'No change to due times. TKT-005 keeps its hours. There are no business hours and no pause.' (115), 'No record of overdue in the log. No event kind is added, and LOG-002 does not change.' (113).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 10 new criteria headed '### PREFIX-NNN: Title': TKT-014..TKT-018 and CLI-010..CLI-014; CLI-001 and CLI-006 edited. check_run: duplicates 0 and testable_lines 0 in both files. Body length, noted not failed: by a rough sentence count 6 of 10 new bodies run past three sentences (TKT-014 7, TKT-017 7, CLI-011 5, CLI-012 5, TKT-015 4, CLI-010 4, 'Assumption, not confirmed' lines included); mean about 56 words.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: cli.md:79-80 (CLI-010) 'In the output of `ticketdesk list`, the line of an overdue ticket is `#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>`, see TKT-014.' Filter: cli.md:97-99 (CLI-011) 'prints one line per overdue ticket, in the order of TKT-017... It prints no line for a ticket that is not overdue.' Order: tickets.md:152-154 (TKT-017) 'It sorts them by due time ascending, so the ticket that has been due longest comes first.' Exact due time: tickets.md:132 (TKT-014) 'At exactly the due time, the ticket is not overdue.' Closed: tickets.md:139 (TKT-015) 'A `closed` ticket is not overdue, whatever its due time and whenever it was closed.' Nothing overdue: cli.md:106 (CLI-012) 'When no ticket is overdue, `ticketdesk overdue` prints nothing and exits with code 0, see CLI-008.'

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: check_run impl_words=0 in both files; no .py name, function, class, or module in any new or edited body. Outcomes are output lines and exit codes, e.g. CLI-013 'prints usage to stderr and exits with code 2. It prints nothing to stdout.' and CLI-014 'prints nothing to stdout and exits with a non-zero code'. Noted, not failed: the assumption lines under CLI-010 to CLI-012 link to the sibling spec file `tickets.md`, a doc cross-reference and not a code file.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: tickets.md:123-124: 'Overdue is derived, never stored. Whether a ticket is overdue follows from the log and the current time alone.' tickets.md:163-165 (TKT-018): 'A ticket that becomes overdue appends no event to the log, and the overdue listing appends nothing, see LOG-001... the log file is byte for byte the same.' Non-goal at 113: 'No event kind is added, and LOG-002 does not change.' INV-001 and INV-002 are not cited by ID (check_run mentions false); the behavior respects both.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-005 reused: tickets.md:131 (TKT-014) 'TKT-005 sets the due time.' and the non-goal at 115. List order kept: cli.md:83 (CLI-010) 'The order of the lines stays the order of TKT-013.' and the non-goal at tickets.md:120 'No change to the order of `list`, see TKT-013.' The due-time order applies only to the overdue listing (TKT-017).

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.

Is a ticket overdue at exactly its due time? Assumed no. Affects TKT-014.' They match questions.md. Inline marks sit under the criteria: tickets.md:135 'Assumption, not confirmed: the rule for the exact due time. See open question 4.'; 143 'Assumption, not confirmed: a ticket closed late is not reported. See open question 1.'; 158 (order and ties); cli.md:92, 101 and 110 for the marker place, the line content, and the exit code. Nothing is resolved silently. Bar used for all six runs: an assumption counts as marked when the spec itself flags it and ties it to the criterion, by a mark under the criterion or by an in-spec list entry that names the criterion ID.

expectations.text: Skim test: the intro paragraph's first sentence says what the feature is for a support agent; each criterion title names the behavior; no lead is a teaser or a qualifier chain.

It says what the feature does for the agent. Titles name behaviors ('A closed ticket is never overdue', 'Assignment does not change overdue', 'Overdue is never recorded', 'OVERDUE marker in list', 'overdue with no overdue ticket', 'overdue on a corrupt log'); 'CLI-011: overdue' is a bare command name in the repo's style and 'Overdue listing' is a label. Every new paragraph lead states a claim; a sweep with the TODO/Assumption prefixes stripped gives 0 teaser findings.
